title: The Pen draws a path, corner by corner and curve by curve
goal: Pick up the Pen and draw. Click to drop a corner, or press and drag to pull a curve out of the point you are placing, the way every vector tool works. Keep going and you see the shape as it will be before you commit each point. Close it by clicking where you started, or finish an open path and get on with the next thing. Someone who has drawn with a pen elsewhere should not have to be told any of this.
notes:
Depends on the path model.

This slice is where "in a natural way" is actually decided, so spend the time on the feel rather than on the feature list. The three things that make a pen feel right or wrong: how far the pointer must travel before a click becomes a drag (too small and every click makes an accidental curve), whether the preview segment tracks the pointer continuously or only updates on press, and whether finishing is obvious. Get those three wrong and every other box on this list can be ticked while the tool is unusable.

Do not add point editing here. Moving, converting and deleting anchors is the next slice; this one is about laying a path down. The exception is undo while drawing, which is in the list because a pen without it is punishing.

Read docs/design/mocks/pages/vector-wt.html and icon-draw-wt.html first, and say in the audit where the mock was followed and where it was not.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for the pen and path set (asked for by the user on 2026-09-13).

The user's words: "I want the ability to draw more complex shapes than a rect - specifically polygons that can do both hard edges and bezier curves in a natural way. This will help us build ellaborate svg icons for example."

Read "in a natural way" as the hard requirement, because it is the part everyone gets wrong. A pen tool is easy to implement and easy to make horrible. The test is that somebody who has used the pen in Figma, Illustrator or Sketch can draw a shape with a straight edge and a curved edge without being taught anything, on their first try, and that somebody who has not used one can still get a triangle out of it. Drag distance, what the handles do while you are still placing a point, and how you finish a path are where that is won or lost.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY. Very little, which is the honest starting position:
- AnnotationShape (Sources/PhotonzCore/Layer.swift:17) is the whole shape vocabulary: arrow, rectangle, highlight, ellipse, line. There is no polygon, no path, and no bezier anything in PhotonzCore or PhotonzRender.
- There is no SVG code anywhere in Sources. Getting paths OUT as SVG is a separate piece of work under the icon-export epic and is deliberately not in this set.
- The key P is already reserved for this. The task 'the-redline-arrow-tool-takes-p-the-key-the-pen-t' is done, and its goal says out loud: "In every other screen of the app, P selects the vector Pen." So the Pen gets P, and the Arrow already moved off it.

THE MOCKS ALREADY SPEC THIS. Read them before designing anything, and treat them as proposals rather than gospel (CLAUDE.md):
- docs/design/mocks/pages/vector-wt.html is the vector walkthrough. Its vocabulary is anchor, path, handle, bezier, and the tasks below use those words on purpose so the app, the mocks and the code agree.
- docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-draw-wt.html is drawing an icon.
- docs/design/mocks/pages/draw-boolean.html covers boolean operations, which are NOT in this set; they are the next thing under icon-vector once a path exists.
- docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md:1276 onwards fixes where the Pen sits in each tool strip, and :1081 says a page showing vector drawing must show the Pen selected.

HOW IT HAS TO FIT THE APP, so a path is a first-class layer and not a special case:
- A path is CONTENT, a new case alongside image, text, annotation and group, not a sixth AnnotationShape. Annotations are two-point marks built from a start and an end (see AnnotationContent); a path has an arbitrary number of anchors and cannot be squeezed into that without breaking everything that assumes two endpoints.
- It paints through the model the whole app already uses: Appearance holds what it HAS (its fill, its outline, its opacity) and Effects is the list you add to (docs/design/shape-parts.md). A path arrives with a fill and an outline like any other shape, takes a saved colour or a gradient like any other shape, and needs no new colour machinery.
- PhotonzCore stays pure: CoreGraphics types only, no CoreImage, no AppKit, everything Sendable, value-typed, Codable, no force unwraps. The path model and every geometry decision belong there and get tested there; only the rasterizer touches CoreGraphics drawing.
- All mutation goes through History.perform, so every anchor added, moved or deleted is undoable.

Queue-driven app work targets the next release, and per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it. Design doc: docs/design/vector-paths.md is the source of truth, written by the foundation task.
acceptance: The Pen is on the tool bar and answers to P, the key already reserved for it
A click drops a corner point; a press and drag pulls handles out of the point being placed, and the curve follows the pointer while the button is down
The segment between the last placed point and the pointer is previewed continuously, so you see the curve you are about to commit before you commit it
Clicking the first point closes the path and the shape fills; Return or Escape finishes an open path, and the two are told apart clearly
The tool hands back the way every other tool does when the path is finished, with the new path selected
Holding Shift constrains the next point to the usual angles
Undo steps back one point at a time while drawing, rather than throwing the whole path away
Drawing a rounded rectangle, a triangle and a shape with one straight edge and one curve each takes no more presses than it would in Figma, counted and recorded in the audit
A first-time check with someone who has never used this pen: they get a closed triangle out without instruction, and what confused them is written down
A playtest walk draws a closed path with a corner and a curve and checks the resulting anchors
Audit under queue/audits/ with each drawing captured step by step, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: deps set: the path model comes first

Adversarial review before building. Walked the flow as someone who has drawn with a pen elsewhere. (1) The first click must leave something visible or you think it failed, so a placed anchor is a dot on the canvas from click one. (2) Closing is guesswork unless the first anchor tells you it is a target: it grows a ring when the pointer is near enough to close, and the click lands on the anchor rather than the pixel. (3) Finishing is the part the mock does worst: vector-wt puts Close path in the Properties panel behind Shift Cmd J, which nobody new will find. Clicking the first anchor closes; Return finishes an open path; clicking the LAST anchor again also finishes, because a mouse-only user never thinks of Return. (4) Escape: the app already means cancel by Escape everywhere (annotation drag, measure placement), so Escape throws the path away and Return keeps it. Those are the two that must be told apart, and the canvas hint says both out loud while you draw. (5) Cut from the mock for this slice: the Path section of Properties (anchor type, node coordinates, Close path button) is the EDITING slice, and node coordinate fields with no way to drag a node are decoration. (6) Shortest version: no anchor editing, no per-path colour capsule on the tool bar (a new path wears the same redline red a new box wears, and Appearance repaints it), no brushes.

Built. PenSession (Sources/PhotonzCore/PenDrawing.swift) holds every decision the gesture makes, 33 tests; CanvasPen.swift draws the chrome and converts view to document; EditorState+Pen.swift commits ONE layer through History.perform. Tool.pen takes P, joins the END of the drawing family behind next-pen. Two walks: pen-draws-a-path-walk (close, undo one point, Escape, Return) and pen-three-drawings-walk (the three shapes the acceptance names). New playtest step expectPath asks the DOCUMENT how many anchors a path has, whether it closed and how many runs are curved, because none of the three can be settled from a picture.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the real app through the probe with Screen Recording granted. What I changed as a result: (1) Shift now re-snaps the preview the moment the key goes down (flagsChanged) rather than at the next mouse move, because holding shift to check a line is level is something you do with the hand already still. (2) Option was added after finding that a rounded rectangle could not be drawn at all: every dragged anchor was smooth with mirrored handles, so the straight edges came out bowed. Option now means one thing in two places (do not tie this anchor’s two sides together) and a rounded rectangle comes out exactly right in fourteen presses. Left rough and written into the audit: the tool hands back to Select after one path, which is what the acceptance asked for and is the first thing to reconsider for icon work; and the chip does not mention Option.

Acceptance, item by item. P and the tool bar: done, and ToolTests now asserts P belongs to the Pen and nothing else. Click a corner / drag a curve: done, drag threshold 4 view points, latched, measured on screen. Continuous preview: done, redrawn on every mouse move in the shape’s own ink. Close by clicking the first point: done, with a ring on the anchor so it is not guesswork; Return keeps the open path, Escape discards it, and the chip is where the two are told apart. Hands back with the path selected: done. Shift: done. Undo one point at a time: done, taken in performKeyEquivalent because a key equivalent never reaches keyDown. Press counts: counted by drawing each shape, recorded in the audit (triangle 4 = Figma 4, straight-plus-curve 4 = 4, rounded rectangle 14 = 14). Walk with anchor checks: done. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-13-pen-draws-a-path.json with three real -sc.png captures.

The one acceptance item a runner cannot close: the first-time check with somebody who has never used this pen. There is no person in an unmanned loop to watch. The audit is written as exactly that check instead: eight steps in order, starting with the triangle, and the first evaluate question is “did you get a closed triangle out on the first try without reading anything”. What confused them gets written down when the user answers on the dashboard.

Asked for a full sweep: the Pen adds a slot to the end of the drawing family, so any walk that clicks the tool bar by coordinate could have shifted. The 15 tool-* walks and both pen walks pass; Scripts/test.sh is green at 6242 tests.
